query_used: 34th New York Infantry regiment history, Company D, Antietam

raw_record.regiment: 34th Regiment, New York Volunteer Infantry ('Herkimer Regiment')
raw_record.organized: Albany, NY; mustered in June 15, 1861, at the Industrial School Barracks, Albany; two-year term
raw_record.left_state: Left Albany for Washington, D.C., July 3, 1861
raw_record.company_D: Recruited from Champlain, Clinton Co.; commander Capt. Davis J. Rich; accepted May 22, 1861 (same day Henry Hubbell enlisted)
raw_record.colonel: William La Due (elected May 30, 1861); Lt. Col. James A. Suiter (commanded at Antietam)
raw_record.antietam_assignment: 1st Brigade (Gorman), 2nd Division (Sedgwick), II Corps (Sumner), Army of the Potomac; commanded on the field by Col. James A. Suiter
raw_record.antietam_action: Sept 17, 1862 — advanced into the West Woods near the Dunker (Dunkard) Church; left flank unprotected after the 127th PA broke; took infantry fire front and both flanks plus artillery on the left; forced to withdraw and reformed on the left of Kirby's battery

candidates.claude_reasoning: Unit-level facts (not person identity). C1 corroboration: the curated assignment '34th NY, Co. D' is confirmed as a real company recruited at Champlain under Capt. Davis J. Rich. The regiment's Antietam role (West Woods, Sedgwick's division) is consistent across DMNA (Phisterer), AOTW, Wikipedia, and the NPS monument. Confidence 'definite' for organization/movement dates (government + multiple corroborating sources).

verified_matches.fact: 34th NY left Albany for Washington July 3, 1861
verified_matches.relevance: Resolves the date of Henry's FIRST letter — see DSC-2026-06-05-001. He could not have 'arrived at Washington' in early June 1861; the regiment had not yet left Albany.

verified_matches.fact: Co. D commander = Capt. Davis J. Rich
verified_matches.relevance: Henry's letters call him 'Capt. Reich' — see DSC-2026-06-05-002 (name-spelling discrepancy, resolved).

verified_matches.fact: 34th NY at Antietam: West Woods, Gorman/Sedgwick/Sumner; ~150 casualties (32 k / 109 w / 9 m) per NY AG & Phisterer
verified_matches.relevance: Battlefield context for Henry's death; the unit lost ~48% of 311 engaged.

notes: A casualty figure DISCREPANCY exists between sources: NY AG/Phisterer give 32 killed / 109 wounded / 9 missing (=150); Wikipedia and the NPS 34th-NY monument inscription give 43 killed / 74 wounded (=117). External-vs-external; recorded in source-quality-notes.md and the discrepancy INDEX (minor). We adopt the NY AG/Phisterer figures as primary.
